```plato

    //==
    // # Warped and derived noise evaluation
    //
    // The `Eval` bodies for `noise.types.plato`: domain warping, which moves
    // the sample point before evaluating the basis, and curl noise, which reads a
    // divergence-free vector field off the derivatives of a scalar (2D) or vector
    // (3D) potential.
    //
    // Iterations is a runtime count and each warp step consumes the PREVIOUS
    // displaced point, so the warp is written as a recursion rather than as the
    // MapRange + Reduce the fractal sums use — the steps do not commute and there is
    // nothing to sum.
    //
    // The curl bodies differentiate by central difference. The step is a fixed
    // 1e-3 in the field's own input units: small enough that the second-order error
    // is invisible next to the noise itself, large enough to stay well clear of
    // catastrophic cancellation in single precision.

    //==
    // # Domain warping
    //
    // Each iteration displaces the point by a warp noise sampled at the point
    // itself, so the field folds through itself repeatedly — the marbling. The
    // two (three) displacement components come from decorrelated seeds; sharing
    // one would displace every point along the diagonal.

    // The point after `remaining` further warp iterations.
    WarpPoint(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, strength: Number, frequency: Number, p: Point2D, remaining: Integer): Point2D
        => remaining <= 0
            ? p
            : WarpPoint(basis, seed, strength, frequency,
                Point2D(p.X + strength * BasisValue2D(basis, seed + 101, frequency, p),
                        p.Y + strength * BasisValue2D(basis, seed + 227, frequency, p)),
                remaining - 1);
```
